# AutoHotkey v2.0.26 for Linux - linux.23

This release closes the two deterministic gaps left open by the linux.22 audit
closure: a packed executable could silently lose optional capabilities, and no
automated test proved a real cross-version upgrade or rollback. The project
remains a technology preview with explicit desktop and long-soak boundaries.

## Highlights

- **Independent broker grab lease.** `ahk-inputd` used to rely on an in-process
  `SIGALRM` handler to release `EVIOCGRAB` when its loop stalled. That handler
  cannot run while the process is `SIGSTOP`ped or wedged in a syscall, so a
  live-but-stopped broker kept every keyboard grabbed and the desktop stopped
  receiving input. Each grabbed device now also has a forked lease process
  (visible as `ahk-inp-lease`) holding a duplicate device fd that releases the
  grab unless the main loop heartbeats within 1.5s; losing supervision fails
  open, and a device whose lease cannot be armed is refused with an explicit
  message instead of being held unsupervised. The `SIGALRM` watchdog stays as a
  second layer. Verified on the VM with an independent grab probe: released
  1358 ms after `SIGSTOP`, released on `SIGKILL` with no lease left behind.
- **Cross-version runtime x daemon matrix.** A new oracle pairs the real
  published linux.19 binaries (whose broker predates protocol v2) with the build
  under test: the old broker is proven v1-only, the new one negotiates v2, all
  four runtime x daemon pairings work, a runtime never reports a healthy or
  granted suppression lane against a broker that cannot grant it, and a live
  runtime survives its broker being swapped to another release without changing
  PID. 18/18 assertions, with the archive and binary SHA-256s recorded in the
  summary.
- **Packed-runtime capability manifest.** `--pack` probes the template it embeds
  (`--pack-info`) instead of assuming it matches this runtime, prints an
  explicit notice when a capability is lost (today: consented libei/EIS
  injection), and embeds a machine-readable manifest naming the release and
  capabilities actually contained in the produced executable. `--version`,
  `--pack-info` and `--diag` report it, and a script sees the same answer
  through `HotkeyBackendGet().libei_build_enabled`. A template that cannot
  declare its capabilities is an explicit error, never a guess.
- **Packed argument contract.** A packed executable forwards its command-line
  words to the embedded script (`A_Args`) instead of treating the first word as
  a replacement script path. `--` forces forwarding, `/script PATH` keeps the
  override, and the binary's own switches still win. `A_IsCompiled` is now 1
  for the whole packed process lifetime, matching upstream Ahk2Exe.
- **Runtime self-identification.** `ahk_core --version` and `--diag` name the
  port release (read from `tools/linux/VERSION` at configure time); previously
  only the launcher knew which release was installed.
- **Cross-version upgrade matrix.** New
  `tests/oracle/run_upgrade_matrix_oracle.sh` proves
  install N-1 -> upgrade to N (while a script keeps running) -> downgrade to
  N-1 -> uninstall -> fresh install of N, including prefix hygiene and the
  launcher's stamped release. `tools/linux/fetch-release-assets.sh` fetches and
  checksum-verifies the real published N-1 assets so CI tests the bytes users
  actually download.
- **Publication gate.** The packaging job now depends on the packed-binary
  container acceptance job, so a green `package` run means every release gate
  for that ref passed rather than a two-job subset.
- **Review-driven hardening.** An independent adversarial review of this
  commit found real defects in the first cut of the lease work, and they were
  fixed before release: lease ownership is now transferred (not copied) when
  device slots compact and a removed device's lease is stopped exactly once;
  lease teardown uses a bounded reap with a `SIGKILL` fallback so a stopped
  lease can no longer block a fail-open transition; a lease that stops draining
  is treated as lost supervision (persistent `EAGAIN` is no longer "healthy")
  and reports degraded health; the lease is armed *before* `EVIOCGRAB`, closing
  the unsupervised acquisition window; the lease child closes descriptors 0-2
  and resets inherited signal dispositions; the pack template path is
  canonicalized so probing and embedding cannot describe different binaries;
  the reserved manifest name is refused as a FileInstall source; the writer
  enforces the reader's 64 MiB bound; a lone `--` forwards zero arguments; and
  `--pack-info` on a packed binary reports the embedded manifest verbatim.
  Two oracle false-pass holes were closed too: the lease budget is now
  1500 + 800 ms with a lease required before the `SIGKILL` case, and the
  cross-version matrix verifies cached assets against `CKSUMS.txt` and requires
  an accepted subscription after the daemon swap.

## Verification

- VM: cross-version matrix PASS (linux.21 -> linux.22 upgrade with a running
  script surviving the interpreter swap, rollback, uninstall, fresh install);
  packed-capability oracle PASS; pack-failure oracle PASS; inputd protocol
  `28/28`; injection `26/26`; headless regression `27/27`.
- VM: inputd lease oracle `11/11`; cross-version runtime x daemon matrix `18/18`.
- Core CI additionally runs the packed-capability oracle, the pack failure
  oracle, the Syntax Studio X11 interaction oracle and the VS Code
  extension-host/DAP oracle, plus the distro container matrix.
- Known limitation carried over: the VM's live desktop session makes the
  `ibus_compat` scenario hang until the runner watchdog kills it. The released
  linux.22 binary behaves identically on that host, so this is an environment
  boundary (CI skips the scenario), not a regression.
- The AUR recipe on the release tag still carries the previous release's
  archive checksum, because a tag archive cannot contain the hash of itself;
  the commit immediately after the tag backfills the published hash.
- Deferred from this release on purpose (they remain open audit items and are
  not claimed as done): the two-device / two-script held-state ownership oracle
  (I03) and the external X11 paste-transaction preservation gate (I05, plus the
  small-payload part of I07).
